whatItDoes.text: Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, accessories and related services.
whatItDoes.quote: The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services.

howItMakesMoney.text: Apple earns revenue from fee‑based services like AppleCare that provide support and coverage.
howItMakesMoney.quote: The Company offers a portfolio of fee‑based service and support products under the AppleCare® brand.

howItMakesMoney.text: Apple also generates advertising revenue through third‑party licensing and its own advertising platforms.
howItMakesMoney.quote: The Company’s advertising services include third‑party licensing arrangements and the Company’s own advertising platforms.

competitiveEdge.text: Apple says it designs and develops almost the entire solution for its products, from hardware to software and services.
competitiveEdge.quote: The Company designs and develops nearly the entire solution for its products, including the hardware, operating system, numerous software applications and related services.

marketPosition.text: Apple says it has a minority market share in the global smartphone, PC, tablet and wearables markets.
marketPosition.quote: The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets

industryTrends.text: Apple notes that its markets are highly competitive and change quickly with new technology.
industryTrends.quote: Global markets for the Company’s products and services are highly competitive and subject to rapid technological change

demandDrivers.text: Apple serves consumers, businesses, education, enterprise and government customers, which drives demand for its products.
demandDrivers.quote: The Company’s customers are primarily in the consumer, small and mid‑sized business, education, enterprise and government markets.

biggestRisks.text: Adverse macroeconomic conditions such as recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates and currency swings can hurt demand.
biggestRisks.quote: Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth or recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates, and currency fluctuations, can adversely impact consumer confidence and spending

biggestRisks.text: Relying on single or limited sources for components exposes Apple to supply shortages and price volatility.
biggestRisks.quote: Because the Company currently obtains certain components from single or limited sources, the Company is subject to significant supply and pricing risks.

biggestRisks.text: Apple says protecting its intellectual property is uneven worldwide, which could weaken its competitive advantage.
biggestRisks.quote: Effective intellectual property protection is not consistently available in every country in which the Company operates.

outlook.text: Apple says future gross margins may vary because of many factors discussed in its risk section.
outlook.quote: The Company’s future gross margins can be impacted by a variety of factors, as discussed in Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K

source.label: 10-K filed October 31, 2025 · Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis

dropped.text: Apple believes its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities will cover its cash needs and capital return program for the next year.
dropped.quote: The Company believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months.

dropped.text: Apple announced iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, visionOS 27, tvOS 27 and introduced Siri AI in Q3 2026.
dropped.quote: During the third quarter of 2026, the Company announced iOS 27, macOS® 27 Golden Gate, iPadOS® 27, watchOS® 27, visionOS® 27 and tvOS® 27, and introduced Siri AI.
